**Given:** The presentations and parameters of the Statement.

[F1] The arbitrary monic cyclotomic Hecke quotients are finite-dimensional by
[[lem-cyclotomic-hecke-bounded-ordered-monomials-span]]. Their mixed and
quadratic relations are those of
[[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]].

[F2] In the KLR presentation, a crossing between distant colors has square
$1$ and interchanges their word idempotents
([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]).
The equal-color native dot moves become $\psi x-y\psi=-1$, $\psi y-x\psi=1$ for $\psi=-\tau$; adjacent unequal quadratic polynomials are $\pm(y-x)$. Finite-dimensionality and nilpotence for this specific integer-line quotient are proved below, rather than imported from a general-Cartan corner assertion.



1.1 Work over a finite splitting extension for the finitely many minimal polynomials of the commuting polynomial generators in the finite regular module of [F1]. Simultaneous primary decomposition gives joint generalized eigenspaces. On such a weight, the first value is a charge root, because the first cyclotomic polynomial annihilates the module. In the degenerate case connect distinct values differing by $1$; in the nondegenerate case connect distinct nonzero values whose ratio is $\xi$ or $\xi^{-1}$. This defines a graph on the distinct values in each word, with at most $d$ vertices. [F1, given, algebra]

1.2 For a KLR word, form the induced line graph on its distinct colors. If a component contains no charge, move its first occurrence left across all earlier letters. These letters lie in other components, so their color differences exceed $1$; [F2] makes every crossing invertible. The resulting word idempotent is nonzero if the original was, but its first color has exponent zero, so the cyclotomic relation kills it. This contradiction shows that each component contains a charge. A component with at most $d$ vertices is an interval, and every color has distance at most $d-1$ from a charge in that component. [F2, given, algebra]

2.1 The mixed relations give intertwiners $\theta_r=s_r(x_r-x_{r+1})+1$ and $\Theta_r=T_r(1-X_rX_{r+1}^{-1})+1-\xi$. Direct multiplication gives $\theta_r^2=1-(x_r-x_{r+1})^2$ and $\Theta_r^2=(1-\xi X_{r+1}X_r^{-1})(1-\xi X_rX_{r+1}^{-1})$; they interchange the two polynomial generators and commute with the others. For example $s_r(x_r-x_{r+1})=-(x_r-x_{r+1})s_r-2$, which yields the first square identity; the second follows by inserting $T_r^2=(\xi-1)T_r+\xi$ and $T_rX_rT_r=\xi X_{r+1}$. Between values in different graph components these squares have nonzero constant terms, hence are invertible on the generalized weight space. Each intertwiner therefore gives an isomorphism onto the swapped generalized weight space. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 **Global dot nilpotence in a finite interval.** At positive level put $N_1=\max_i\lambda_i\ge1$. The first-strand relations give $y_1^{N_1}=0$ in the ENTIRE finite-window quotient, since uncharged first colors already have zero idempotent and every charged exponent is at most $N_1$. Suppose globally $y_a^N=0$. On an equal pair put $x=y_a$, $y=y_{a+1}$, $\delta=x-y$, $\psi=-\tau_a$, and $\Phi=1+\delta\psi$. The mixed identities give $\psi\delta=-\delta\psi-2$, $\psi^2=0$, hence $\Phi^2=1$ and $\Phi x=y\Phi$. Therefore $y^Ne(\nu)=\Phi x^N\Phi e(\nu)=0$. On an unequal pair, multiplying the GLOBAL relation by crossings gives $0=\psi y_a^N\psi e(\nu)=y_{a+1}^NQ_{\nu_a\nu_{a+1}}(y_a,y_{a+1})e(\nu)$. This uses the annihilator in the swapped corner as well, which is justified by its global hypothesis. Distant colors have $Q=1$, giving $y^N=0$. Adjacent colors have $Q=\pm(y-x)$, giving $y^{N+1}=xy^N$; raising that commuting-polynomial identity to the Nth power gives $y^{N(N+1)}=x^Ny^{N^2}=0$. Thus the common global exponent $N_{a+1}=N_a(N_a+1)$ works on EVERY word. Induction proves nilpotence of all dots, without assuming a supported corner is the full algebra or transporting a corner-only annihilator through another color. [F2, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 Suppose a component contains no charge root. Its earliest occurrence in the word can be moved to the first position by the invertible swaps of step 2.1: every preceding value belongs to a different component. The resulting nonzero weight space has an uncharged first value, contradicting the first cyclotomic relation. Consequently each component contains a charge root. A simple path from that root to any vertex has length at most $d-1$, so the value is an integer within $d-1$ of an integral charge, respectively a power $\xi^a$ with $|a-m_j|\le d-1$. Infinite order of $\xi$ makes the integer labels unique. All spectral values therefore belong to $k$, and their polynomial primary projectors descend to $k$ by the Chinese remainder identity. [step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 **Finite dimension and genuine full-line windows.** Move dots past crossings using the mixed relations. Repeated crossings reduce by the quadratic relation; braid changes to fixed reduced words have corrections with fewer crossings. Adjacent-transposition sorting supplies the symmetric-group word reductions, so induction on crossing count expresses every element as a finite sum of $\psi_wy^ae(\nu)$ for the finitely many permutations w and window words $\nu$. Step 2.2 reduces all exponents to $a_r<N_r$, giving finite-dimensionality of each finite-window content quotient. Only finitely many words satisfy the support bound of step 1.2. Each full-line content presentation uses only its own colors: permutations of a word and every local relation preserve its content. Thus a content wholly within the bound has exactly the same generators AND all relations in every sufficiently large interval; omitted contents have every word idempotent zero by step 1.2. Their whole content algebras are zero because those finitely many idempotents are their identity. Hence the full rank algebra is exactly the finite direct sum of surviving content quotients, not a selected supported corner. Enlarging a window creates only zero entire content algebras and changes no old relation. This proves the claimed equality and finite-dimensionality. [F2, step 1.2, step 2.2, algebra]

4.1 **Hecke nilpotent dots, descent and zero boundaries.** Step 3.1 places every Hecke spectral value in k. On its finite regular module the local differences $y_re(\nu)=(x_r-\nu_r)e(\nu)$ or $(1-\xi^{-\nu_r}X_r)e(\nu)$ are nilpotent by primary decomposition. The finitely many orthogonal commuting projectors sum to one, so their componentwise differences combine to globally commuting nilpotent dots with a common finite exponent in each rank. The primary projector is a polynomial in the generators, defined over k by the Chinese remainder identity; it acts in every representation because the regular-module polynomial annihilators hold as algebra identities. At level zero the first polynomial is1 and every positive Hecke rank is zero; every KLR word has first exponent zero and is likewise killed. Rank zero is k. Together with steps 3.1 and 3.2 this proves all support, finite-dimensionality, nilpotence and window conclusions without a Hecke–KLR isomorphism or a cyclotomic polynomial faithfulness claim. [F1, F2, step 3.1, step 3.2, algebra] ∎

**Given:** The arbitrary-base nondegenerate affine presentation of [[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]] specialized to k and q, and the finite-window KLR presentation of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] with the displayed line Q. Their central local completions are derived from these actual presented affine algebras in steps 5.1, 6.1, 7.1. The integer-color local presentations are as stated. Their coefficient ring is the direct sum of one formal power-series ring per color word; no finite-$e$ definition or comparison theorem is being instantiated. In the Hecke presentation the spectral idempotents are the projections to these local rings. Multiplication by $X_r$ on its $i$-summand is $q^{i_r}(1-y_r)$. The usual affine Hecke relations are $T_r^2=(q-1)T_r+q$, $T_rX_rT_r=qX_{r+1}$, and the braid and distant commutation relations.



**Given:** The displayed presentations and the formal series $P,Q$.

1.1 All coefficients are legal. For $a\ne b$, $x-z$ has constant $q^a-q^b\ne0$. In the last case of $Q$, $x-qz$ has nonzero constant because $a\ne b+1$. In the backward case $-q^a/(x-z)$ is a unit. In the equal case $1-q\ne0$. Thus every denominator is a unit and each $Q$ is a unit. The formulas depend only on the adjacent pair, so they make sense in every rank and in every finite color window. [given, algebra]



1.2 Use an explicit polynomial representation. On the $i$-component let dots multiply, and let a permutation simultaneously permute coordinates and colors. With $\partial_r=(s_r-1)/(y_r-y_{r+1})$, define $\psi_r$ on an equal pair to be $\partial_r$; on an unequal source pair $(a,b)$ let its output in the swapped component be $h_{ab}(u,v)s_r$, where $h_{ab}(u,v)=v-u$ if $a=b+1$ and $h_{ab}=1$ otherwise. The equal-color quotient is a power series because the numerator vanishes on $u=v$. Its product rule is $\partial(fg)=\partial(f)g+(sf)\partial(g)$. Consequently $\partial v=u\partial+1$, $v\partial=\partial u+1$, and $\partial^2=0$. On unequal pairs the square is multiplication by $h_{ba}(u,v)h_{ab}(v,u)=K_{ab}(u,v)$. These computations verify all mixed and quadratic relations, including the native sign $\tau=-\psi$. [given, algebra]



2.1 Three distinct colors. In both three-crossing words the coefficient of the longest permutation is the product of the three pair factors, transported to the same coordinates. Each pair is crossed once. The factors commute and $s_1s_2s_1=s_2s_1s_2$, so the two words agree. This argument does not require nonadjacency; some of the factors can be linear. [step 1.2, algebra]



2.2 First two colors equal. For $(a,a,b)$ write $h=h_{ab}$. The left word is $h(u,v)h(u,w)s_1s_2\partial_1$, and the right word is $\partial_2h(u,v)h(u,w)s_1s_2$. The product of factors is invariant under swapping $v,w$, so its $\partial_2$ is zero. Also $\partial_2s_1s_2=s_1s_2\partial_1$ by conjugating the displayed quotient. The words agree. For $(a,b,b)$ the left word is $\partial_1h(v,w)h(u,w)s_2s_1$, and the right word is $h(v,w)h(u,w)s_2s_1\partial_2$. Here the product is invariant under swapping $u,v$, and $\partial_1s_2s_1=s_2s_1\partial_2$. This verifies the third color pattern separately. [step 1.2, algebra]



2.3 Outer colors equal. On $(a,b,a)$ with $a\ne b$, put $h=h_{ab}$ and $g=h_{ba}$. Expanding the one equal-color crossing gives left and right words $\frac{g(u,v)}{u-w}\bigl(h(v,w)s_1s_2s_1-h(v,u)\bigr),\qquad\frac{h(v,w)}{u-w}\bigl(g(u,v)s_2s_1s_2-g(w,v)\bigr).$ Their longest-permutation terms cancel. Their difference is $[K_{ab}(w,v)-K_{ab}(u,v)]/(u-w)$, the stated braid correction. This equals $1$ when $b=a+1$, $-1$ when $a=b+1$, and zero otherwise. Thus the apparent denominator cancels identically. [step 1.2, algebra]



2.4 All three colors equal. Put $D=(u-v)(u-w)(v-w)$. Expanding the quotients and collecting each of the six permutations gives $\partial_1\partial_2\partial_1=\partial_2\partial_1\partial_2=-D^{-1}\sum_{t\in S_3}\operatorname{sgn}(t)t.$ The numerator is alternating and hence divisible by each of the three pair differences, so this is an operator on power series. This explicitly supplies the all-equal case omitted as an exercise in the source. Together with steps 2.1, 2.2, 2.3 it proves all five braid patterns. [step 1.2, algebra]



2.5 Compute the Hecke generators in the same representation. At an output component set $U=X_r$, $V=X_{r+1}$. For unequal colors the swapped input series $Q$ times $h$ is $(qU-V)/(U-V)$: in the backward case $qU-V=q^a(v-u)$, and the swapped input series is $-q^a/(V-U)=q^a/(U-V)$, so multiplying by $h=v-u$ gives exactly the stated coefficient. In every other unequal case this is the last row of $Q$ directly. Also $-P=(1-q)V/(U-V)$. For equal colors, expand $\partial Q-1$; its permutation coefficient is $(1-q+qu-v)/(u-v)$ and its identity coefficient is $-(1-q)(1-v)/(u-v)$. Thus in every case $T_r=A(U,V)s_r+B(U,V),\qquad A(U,V)=\frac{qU-V}{U-V},\quad B(U,V)=\frac{(1-q)V}{U-V}.$ The equal-color poles cancel on power series, as follows already from $T=\partial Q-1$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]



3.1 Mixed and quadratic Hecke identities. Write $A_{ij}=A(X_i,X_j)$ and $B_{ij}=B(X_i,X_j)$. Direct common-denominator expansion gives $B_{ij}+B_{ji}=q-1$, $A_{ij}=q-B_{ij}$, and $A_{ij}A_{ji}=q+(q-1)B_{ij}-B_{ij}^2$. Squaring $A_{ij}s+B_{ij}$ therefore gives $(q-1)T+q$. The identity $TX_i-X_{i+1}T=(1-q)X_{i+1}$ follows by cancellation of its permutation term. Combining this identity with the quadratic identity gives $TX_iT=qX_{i+1}$. Distant commutations follow from disjoint variables. [step 2.5, algebra]



4.1 The Hecke braid holds in every color pattern, including all equal. Set $c=q-1$. Clearing the three pair denominators gives the rational identity $B_{13}(c-B_{12}-B_{23})+B_{12}B_{23}=0$. The coefficients of the longest permutation, $s_1s_2$, and $s_2s_1$ in $T_1T_2T_1$ are $A_{12}A_{13}A_{23}$, $A_{12}A_{13}B_{23}$, and $B_{12}A_{23}A_{13}$; the right word has the same coefficients. The $s_1$ coefficients are $A_{12}(B_{13}B_{21}+B_{12}B_{23})$ and $A_{12}B_{23}B_{13}$; the displayed identity makes them equal. The $s_2$ comparison is its transposed version. The identity coefficients differ by $(B_{12}-B_{23})\bigl(B_{13}(c-B_{12}-B_{23})+B_{12}B_{23}\bigr)=0.$ This uses the quadratic product identity of step 3.1. These are all six permutations, so the braid is proved. It is a rational identity before any color specialization; the equal-color operators preserve power series by step 2.5. [step 2.5, step 3.1, algebra]



5.1 **Faithful actual affine Hecke presentation before completion or quotient.** Work first over $C=k[X_1^{\pm1},\ldots,X_d^{\pm1}]$, not over a cyclotomic quotient or an assumed local algebra. On its rational function field use $T_r=A(X_r,X_{r+1})s_r+B(X_r,X_{r+1})$, whose mixed, quadratic and full six-permutation braid identities were proved in steps 3.1–4.1. The action preserves C: $T_rf=(s_rf)T_r+B(f-s_rf)$, and the difference $f-s_rf$ is divisible by $X_r-X_{r+1}$ for Laurent monomials, then all Laurent polynomials. This formula also follows in the actual affine presentation from its generator mixed relation by its product rule. It moves coefficients past crossings; Coxeter word reductions using the quadratic and braid relations span by $T_wf(X)$ with chosen reduced words w. In the rational action, $T_w$ has the product of the transported nonzero A factors times its own permutation w, and other terms have strictly shorter permutation length. Distinct variable permutations are independent over the rational field: a minimal nonzero relation evaluated on fg minus a selected permutation's value on g times its evaluation on f gives a shorter nonzero relation, choosing a coordinate g on which two permutations differ. Hence these spanning words are independent and the affine presented algebra is finite free of rank d! as a right C-module. This proves actual affine faithfulness BEFORE local completion and before any cyclotomic quotient; no specialization or generic-rank dimension argument is used. [given, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 **Faithful actual affine KLR presentation.** On the finite word set the polynomial operators in step 1.2 satisfy the native dot/quadratic relations and all FIVE equality patterns of three colors by steps 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4. Move dots to the right, then reduce crossing words to fixed reduced permutation words. A repeated crossing is a polynomial by its square relation; a braid replacement has a polynomial correction with fewer crossings. The adjacent-transposition sorting proof of the symmetric-group Coxeter reductions thus gives finite spanning words $\psi_wf(y)e(\nu)$. In the direct sum of the rational-function fields of the word components, each such crossing word has a nonzero polynomial-or-divided-difference leading coefficient times its permutation w, and all other terms have shorter permutation length. Isolate an input and output component; distinct permutations stabilizing those components remain distinct automorphisms of their independent dot variables. The minimal-relation argument of step 5.1 makes these leading permutations independent. Descend through crossing length to prove the displayed spanning words independent. Hence this is a faithful representation of the actual affine KLR presentation and gives its finite coefficientwise PBW module. Fractions are only used to prove independence of regular polynomial operators, not to invert dots in the presented algebra. [given, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 2.4, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 **Genuine central completions and spectral projectors.** Fix one spectral multiset $\beta$ and let J in the symmetric Laurent polynomial center be generated by $f(X)-f(q^\beta)$. Symmetric coefficients are central by step 5.1's mixed formula. Each coordinate in C/JC is a root of $\prod_{i\in\beta}(t-q^i)$, so this coefficient quotient is finite-dimensional and its geometric points are exactly the permutations of that multiset. All points lie over k. Its radical is the intersection of the corresponding finitely many maximal ideals; the finite-dimensional quotient has nilpotent radical, so its powers are cofinal with the powers of JC. Chinese remainders identify the coefficient completion with $\bigoplus_{\nu\in\operatorname{Orb}(\beta)}k[\![y_1,\ldots,y_d]\!]e(\nu)$, with $X_r=q^{\nu_r}(1-y_r)$. Step 5.1's affine PBW module then identifies the ACTUAL central completion with the same finite sum of PBW words and formal coefficients, and its spectral projectors are the displayed completed coefficient idempotents. On the KLR side the positive symmetric dot polynomials are central by the equal divided-difference rule and unequal permutation rule. Their ideal has radical $(y_1,\ldots,y_d)$: each $y_r^d$ belongs to that symmetric ideal by the characteristic-polynomial identity, giving cofinal powers explicitly. Step 6.1 therefore gives its actual central completion as the same finite formal PBW module. A finite permutation-stable set with several contents is the finite direct sum of these completions; distinct spectral multisets give comaximal central ideals. Formal multiplication is legitimate: a permutation preserves dot order and each divided difference lowers it by at most one, while the finite PBW crossing lengths give uniform finite order loss. The faithful rational triangular argument continues over the fraction fields of the formal rings. Thus both completions have the coefficient ring assumed in the local formulas, with actual polynomial spectral projectors and continuous multiplication, independently of any cyclotomic faithfulness assertion. [given, step 1.2, step 5.1, step 6.1, algebra]



8.1 Both directions and both composites. In the faithful KLR action, steps 2.5–4.1 prove the Hecke relations of the displayed inverse generators. In the faithful local Hecke action, solving step 2.5 gives precisely the polynomial crossings of step 1.2, whose relations were proved in steps 1.2 and 2.1–2.4. Since $Q$ is a unit, the two operator subalgebras generated by coefficients and their respective crossings coincide. Thus the presentations are isomorphic. On idempotents and dots the two composites are the identity by the spectral decomposition and $X_r=q^{i_r}(1-y_r)$. On crossings the composite is $(\psi_rQ-P+P)Q^{-1}=\psi_r$; on Hecke crossings it is $(T_r+P)Q^{-1}Q-P=T_r$. These are ordered products; no coefficient has been commuted past a crossing. This completes the local inverse comparison in both directions. [step 1.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, step 7.1, construct] ∎

**Given:** The parameters, presentations, and the following two proved
supplier contracts, whose exact presentation binding is checked below.

[F1] [[lem-generic-cyclotomic-type-a-support-is-bounded-by-rank]] supplies the support theorem: at positive level, the algebras in rank $d>0$ are finite-dimensional, their dots are
nilpotent, and every surviving color lies in
$B_d=[\min S-d+1,\max S+d-1]\cap\mathbb Z$. Hecke joint spectral
projectors $e_H(\nu)$ exist over $k$, with eigenvalues $\nu_r$ or
$\xi^{\nu_r}$. The full-line KLR rank algebra is unchanged by any finite
interval containing $B_d$. At level zero all positive ranks are zero and
rank zero is $k$.

[F2] There are fixed pairwise formal series $p_{ab},q_{ab},P_{ab},Q_{ab}$
for every $a,b\in\mathbb Z$, independent of rank, multicharge, content and
window; $q_{ab},Q_{ab}$ are units. On every finite integer window, the local
replacements displayed in the Statement satisfy all affine mixed,
quadratic, distant and braid relations in both directions, with the same
KLR convention. This contract is proved locally by
[[lem-integer-color-degenerate-hecke-klr-local-inverse-tables]] and
[[lem-generic-nondegenerate-local-inverse-tables]], including all five equality
patterns of three colors in the same native convention $\psi=-\tau$; the
cited article and a finite-$e$ instantiation do not replace these local proofs. The first direction
uses the actual Hecke joint projectors and dots; the reverse uses the KLR
word idempotents and dots. No cyclotomic relation, inverse composite,
spectral identification or tower assertion is assumed in this input.



1.1 **Bind the actual proved suppliers.** The arbitrary-base affine presentations in the Statement specialize the common defining generators and relations over k, with first-strand monic polynomials $\prod_j(t-m_j)$ and $\prod_j(t-\xi^{m_j})$; the latter has unit constant term. Thus the finite-dimensional spanning and spectral-support proof [F1] applies at every level and rank. Its line datum satisfies the native quadratic symmetry and homogeneous extremal conditions with $d_i=1$, and its standard exponents are exactly $\lambda_i=\#\{j:m_j=i\}$. On every finite interval its support proof gives actual whole-algebra equality, global nilpotent dots and polynomial projectors over k, not just a supported corner. The two local suppliers in [F2] use the SAME native $\tau$ and set $\psi=-\tau$: both have $\psi u-v\psi=-1$, $\psi v-u\psi=1$, quadratic $Q_{a,a+1}=v-u$, $Q_{a+1,a}=u-v$, and braid difference $\psi_1\psi_2\psi_1-\psi_2\psi_1\psi_2=[Q(u,v)-Q(w,v)]/(w-u)$ on $(a,b,a)$. Their pair series are fixed for all integer pairs and all ranks; the nondegenerate symbol q is our $\xi$. Their proofs give faithful ACTUAL affine polynomial presentations before completion and before any quotient, then identify the true central completions with one formal dot ring per word. They prove both map directions on all five equality patterns of three colors, including all equal, and inverse composites with the displayed right multiplication order. Therefore they apply to exactly the affine blocks under consideration; no finite cyclic quantum characteristic, generic-rank faithfulness or cyclotomic polynomial faithfulness is assumed. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

2.1 Evaluate a formal series in commuting nilpotent dots by its finite Taylor sum. This evaluation is independent of the nilpotence exponent chosen: every larger truncation differs only by zero monomials. A series with nonzero constant term is a unit by a terminating geometric expansion. Thus all replacements in the Statement are defined. By [F1] only finitely many words survive in any rank. The local relation verifications in [F2], applied on those words, give homomorphisms between the affine presentations before checking the first-strand quotient. No cyclic wraparound or reduction of integer colors is used. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 On a first color $i$, write the degenerate cyclotomic polynomial as $f(i+y)=y^{\lambda_i}U_i(y)$, where $U_i(y)=\prod_{m_j\ne i}(i-m_j+y)$. Its constant term is nonzero in characteristic zero. In the other branch $g(\xi^i(1-y))=(-\xi^i)^{\lambda_i}y^{\lambda_i}V_i(y)$, where $V_i(y)=\prod_{m_j\ne i}(\xi^i-\xi^{m_j}-\xi^iy)$. Infinite multiplicative order makes its constant term nonzero. Both auxiliary factors are units after nilpotent evaluation. Thus the Hecke cyclotomic relation on each projector is equivalent to $y_1^{\lambda_i}e(i,\ldots)=0$. If $\lambda_i=0$, the unit polynomial kills the entire projector. This proves both directions of cyclotomic IDEAL transport: in each completed word corner the transformed Hecke generator is an invertible scalar and unit power series times $y_1^{\lambda_i}e(i,\ldots)$. Multiplication by that factor gives containment in the KLR-generated two-sided ideal; multiplication by its inverse gives the reverse containment. Summing the finitely many orthogonal first-color corners proves equality of the full two-sided ideals. On either nilpotent quotient these units evaluate by finite Taylor sums, so the actual affine maps descend to homomorphisms of the entire cyclotomic algebras in both directions. This does not assume that a restricted supported subalgebra is the full quotient. [given, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Denote the descended reverse map by $\sigma_d:H_d\to R_d^\lambda$. On $e_R(\nu)R_d^\lambda$, each $\sigma_d(x_r)$ has sole generalized eigenvalue $\nu_r$, or $\sigma_d(X_r)$ has sole generalized eigenvalue $\xi^{\nu_r}$. Distinct colors have distinct values, and the orthogonal word idempotents sum to one. The simultaneous primary projector is therefore precisely left multiplication by $e_R(\nu)$. The Hecke polynomial projector maps to this idempotent: its Chinese-remainder polynomial is one modulo the corresponding primary factors and zero modulo all other factors. Hence $\sigma_d(e_H(\nu))=e_R(\nu)$. The forward map already sends $e_R(\nu)$ to $e_H(\nu)$. [F1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Both composites fix the word projectors by step 4.1 and the dots by direct substitution $x_r-\nu_r=y_r$, or $1-\xi^{-\nu_r}X_r=y_r$. On a word, the crossing composite is $(\psi_rq_{ab}-p_{ab}+p_{ab})q_{ab}^{-1}=\psi_r$, or $(\psi_rQ_{ab}-P_{ab}+P_{ab})Q_{ab}^{-1}=\psi_r$. Conversely the Hecke composite sends $s_re_H(\nu)$ to $((s_r+p_{ab})q_{ab}^{-1}q_{ab}-p_{ab})e_H(\nu)=s_re_H(\nu)$; the formula with $T,P,Q$ is identical. The polynomial generators are fixed, and the units $X_r^{-1}$ are fixed because inverses are unique. Thus the homomorphisms are inverse on every generator, without commuting a crossing through its series. [step 2.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 For ranks through $D>0$ at positive level use the common interval $W_D=[\min S-D,\max S+D]\cap\mathbb Z$. It contains the support through rank $D$ and one unused ghost color beyond each endpoint of $B_D$. A crossing permutes existing colors and never creates one; nevertheless these endpoint colors keep every boundary edge of a surviving color represented by the integer-line convention. For operations reaching rank $D+t$, use $W_{D+t}$, and enlarge further to contain any specified color and its neighbors. All extra word idempotents vanish by [F1]. Since [F2] fixes the same series for each ordered pair in every interval, evaluation on surviving words is unchanged by enlargement. The resulting maps are independent of windows and glue across all finite rank bounds. [F1, F2, step 5.1, construct]

7.1 Let $\iota_H:H_d\to H_{d+1}$ send each existing Hecke generator to the generator with the same index. It is a homomorphism because all rank-$d$ relations, including the first-strand relation, hold in rank $d+1$. Its spectral projector satisfies $\iota_H(e_H(\nu))=\sum_a e_H(\nu,a)$: the first $d$ polynomial generators give a representation of $H_d$ on the rank-$d+1$ regular module, so their primary projector is the sum of exactly these joint projectors. The minimal polynomial of each rank-d algebra generator on its regular module annihilates that algebra element itself, hence every representation of $H_d$; the same is true of the polynomial primary projectors. Thus the first-d primary decomposition on the rank-d+1 regular module contains exactly the rank-d allowed eigenvalues, and every prefix violating rank-d support is zero. This is the algebra-identity consequence of [F1], rather than an unsupported extension of a regular-module assertion. This argument also holds for $d=0$, where the empty projector is one. [F1, given, step 6.1, algebra]
